text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 0.66% today to $427.55, continuing a sharper two-week decline of 10%. The stock moved lower on the day the company reported quarterly earnings and announced a leadership change, though the financial report itself isn't detailed in the available data. The broader energy sector has shown caution ahead of earnings season, with analysts warning that while Big Oil profits are expected to surge, guidance from refiners and producers may disappoint investors looking for confidence in future performance.

Refining margins remain under pressure despite relatively tight market conditions: US crude is trading at $103/barrel while global crude sits higher at $123/barrel, and refineries are running at 92.8% capacity with modest inventory levels. This spread between domestic and global prices, combined with a shift in political winds—Democratic control of Congress could favor renewable energy over fossil fuels—may be weighing on investor sentiment for traditional refining plays.
